subject: geography
title: Weather & Climate Adventure: Extreme Weather
welcome_lead: Beast from the East, Storm Desmond, summer heatwaves — is UK weather getting more extreme?
meta_desc: GCSE Geography extreme weather — UK case studies, climate change, evidence.
final_note: You explored UK extreme weather case studies and the evidence for climate change.

concepts.def: Weather very different from the average
Prolonged period of unusually hot weather
Long-term shift in global climate patterns
Heat trapped by gases in the atmosphere
Action to reduce causes of climate change

walkthroughs.body_html:
Storm Desmond (Dec 2015): record rainfall in Cumbria, severe flooding in Carlisle.

Beast from the East (Feb 2018): Polar continental air brought heavy snow, ~17 deaths.

Heatwave July 2022: UK hit 40.3°C at Coningsby — first ever 40°C reading.

Global temperatures have risen ~1.1°C since 1880.

Evidence: shrinking Arctic sea ice, retreating glaciers, rising sea levels (~20cm since 1900), earlier spring blossoms, ice cores showing rising CO2.

Causes: burning fossil fuels, deforestation, agriculture (methane) — all increase greenhouse gases.

Mitigation: renewables, carbon capture, reforestation, international agreements (Paris 2015).

Adaptation: flood defences, drought-resistant crops, changing building design.

mcqs.q: What did the UK record for the first time during the July 2022 heatwave?
options: Hottest summer overall
A temperature of 40°C or above
No rainfall for a year
A tornado

mcqs.q: Which is an example of climate change MITIGATION (not adaptation)?
options: Building higher flood walls
Switching to renewable energy
Air conditioning new homes
Drought-resistant crops

mcqs.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
options: Weather happens outside and climate happens globally.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Weather is short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place; climate is the long-term (typically 30-year) average of weather patterns in a region.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.
Climate change only happens in summer.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.
The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.
Climate change only happens in summer.
